question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{11}{6},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{27}, & 0<x<3, \\ \frac{9}{{x}^{4}}, & 3\le x, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{8}{27}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{9}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{8{x}^{2}}{27}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{9}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{8{x}^{3}}{81}|}_{0}^{3}+{(-\frac{9}{x})|}_{3}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{17}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{17}{3}-{(\frac{11}{6})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{83}{36} \\  & ≈2.31\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.
